Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 62, verse 1–2:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Mighty, the Wise (1)﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Everything in the seven heavens and everything in the earths of His creation glorifies Allah and magnifies Him, willingly and unwillingly. ﴿The Sovereign, the Pure﴾: the One to whom belongs the dominion of this world and the Hereafter and their authority, whose command is executed in the heavens and the earth and what is in them. Al-Quddus (the Pure): He is free of everything that the polytheists attribute to Him and describe Him by, of what is not among His attributes; the Blessed. ﴿Al-Aziz﴾ means the Mighty in His vengeance against His enemies. ﴿Al-Hakim﴾ (the Wise) in His management of His creation and His disposing of them in what He knows best of their interests.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and the wisdom, although they were before that in clear error (2)﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Allah is the One who sent among the unlettered (al-ummiyyin) a messenger from among them. The pronoun in "huwa" refers to the Name of Allah. The unlettered (al-ummiyyun) are the Arabs. We have already explained earlier the reason for which the unlettered person is called ummi.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said regarding "the unlettered" in this place.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves﴾: "The Arabs."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri narrate, I do not know it except from Mujahid, that he said: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses﴾: "The Arabs."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves﴾, he said: This tribe of the Arabs was an unlettered nation, having no book that they read, so Allah sent His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) as a mercy and guidance by which He guides them.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves﴾, he said: This nation was unlettered, not reading any book.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves﴾: "The community of Muhammad (ﷺ) was only called the unlettered because no book was revealed to them." And His words, majestic is His praise, ﴿a messenger from among them﴾ mean from among the unlettered, and He said "from among them" because Muhammad (ﷺ) was unlettered and emerged from the Arabs.

* *

As for His words: ﴿reciting to them His verses﴾

He, majestic is His praise, says: He recites to these unlettered people the verses of Allah that He revealed to him. ﴿And purifying them﴾ means: and He purifies them from the filth of disbelief.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and teaching them the Book﴾

He says: and He teaches them the Book of Allah, and what is in it of the command and prohibition of Allah and the laws of His religion. ﴿And the wisdom﴾: by wisdom is meant the sunnah (the prophetic practice).

The people of interpretation have said what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and teaching them the Book and the wisdom﴾: that is, the sunnah.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, saying: ﴿and purifying them and teaching them the Book and the wisdom﴾, also, as He taught these, He purifies them with the Book and righteous deeds, and teaches them the Book and the wisdom, as He did with the earlier ones. He recited the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in excellence﴾, among those who remained of the people of Islam until the Hour comes. He said: Allah has placed among them foremost ones. He recited the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost, those are the ones brought near﴾, and He said: ﴿A multitude from the earlier peoples and a few from the later ones﴾. So the multitude of the earlier ones are foremost, and the few of the later ones are foremost. He recited: ﴿And the companions of the right, what are the companions of the right﴾ until He reached ﴿a multitude from the earlier peoples and a multitude from the later ones﴾ also. He said: The foremost among the earlier ones are more numerous, and among the later ones few. He recited ﴿And those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith﴾, the verse, and said: These are of the people of Islam until the Hour comes.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And indeed they were before that in clear error﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: These unlettered people had been before Allah sent among them a messenger from among them in deviation from the right path and in going astray, following other than guidance, clear (mubin), meaning: it is evident to whoever reflects upon it that it is error and deviation from the truth and the path of right guidance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 62, verse 3–4:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ (3) ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾ (4)

Say: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: It is He who sent among the Unlettered (al-ummiyyin) a messenger from among them, and among others from among them who have not yet joined them. So "others" (ākharīn) is in the genitive position, in conjunction with "the Unlettered."

The scholars have differed concerning those meant by His saying, ﴿and others among them﴾. Some of them said: it refers to the non-Arabs (al-ʿajam).

Mention of those who said this:

Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, he said: They are the non-Arabs.

Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbuʿi related to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Talhah related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, he said: They are the non-Arabs.

Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, he said: The non-Arabs.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAsim related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, he said: The non-Arabs.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri, whom I know only from Mujahid: ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, he said: The non-Arabs.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Maʿin related to us, saying: Hisham ibn Yusuf related to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-ʿAs, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ibn ʿUmar, that he said to him: Indeed, Surat al-Jumuʿah was revealed concerning us and you, concerning your killing of the liar. Then he recited, ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah…﴾ until he reached ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, and said: You are they.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, he said: The non-Arabs.

Muhammad ibn Maʿmar related to me, saying: Abu ʿAmir related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz related to us; and Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, both from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when Surat al-Jumuʿah was revealed to him. When he recited, ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, a man said: Who are these, O Messenger of Allah? The Prophet ﷺ did not answer him until he asked once, twice, or three times. Among us was Salman al-Farisi, so the Prophet ﷺ placed his hand on Salman and said: 'If faith were at the Pleiades, men from these would reach it.'"

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal al-Madani related to us, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Salim Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: And we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned something similar.

Others said: What is meant by it is everyone who entered Islam after the Prophet ﷺ, whoever they were, until the Day of Resurrection.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, he said: Whoever follows Islam among all people.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, he said: These are everyone who came after the Prophet ﷺ until the Day of Resurrection, everyone who entered Islam from among the Arabs and the non-Arabs.

The most correct of the two views in my opinion is the view of the one who said: What is meant by it is every later person who joins those who accompanied the Prophet ﷺ in their Islam, of whatever lineage; because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, generalized by His saying, ﴿and others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, every later joiner from among the others, and did not single out one kind over another. So every one who joins them is from "the others," who were not among the first ones to whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the verses of Allah.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿who have not yet joined them﴾:

He says: They have not yet come, but they will come.

Those in the field of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying, ﴿who have not yet joined them﴾: meaning, they have not come yet.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾:

He says: And Allah is Exalted in Might in His retribution against those among them who disbelieved in Him, Wise in His management of His creation.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: This which He, may His remembrance be exalted, did by sending a messenger among the Unlettered from the Arabs, and among others from among them, reciting to them His verses and doing all that is described, is the bounty of Allah, which He bestowed upon these people and not others. He gives it to whom He wills: that is, He gives His bounty to whomever He wills of His creation. Whoever He withholds it from does not deserve blame, because He did not withhold from him a right that was his, nor did He wrong him by diverting it from him to another; rather, it is given to those who are worthy of it, so He entrusts it to them and places it with them.

Those in the field of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us, from Shabib, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding: ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾, he said: The bounty is the religion. ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾: meaning, Allah is the Possessor of bounty toward His servants, the righteous among them and the sinful, and those among whom the Messenger was sent from among them and others, the Great, whose bounty every possessor of bounty regards as small in comparison to His.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books. Wretched is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (5)

He, dhikruhu (may His remembrance be exalted), says: the likeness of those who were given the Torah from among the Jews and the Christians, who took up the work of it, ﴿then did not carry it﴾ means: then did not act upon what is in it, and denied Muhammad ﷺ, though they had been commanded in it to believe in him, follow him, and affirm him. ﴿Like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾ means: like a donkey that carries on its back books of knowledge, from which it gains nothing and does not understand what is in them. Likewise, those who were given the Torah, in which the matter of Muhammad ﷺ is made clear, their likeness, when they do not benefit from what is in it, is like the donkey that carries books containing knowledge, while it neither understands them nor benefits from them.

Those of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿carrying books﴾ he said: he carries books and does not know what is in them, nor does he understand them.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾ he said: he carries a book and does not know what is upon it nor what is in it.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾ he said: like the donkey that carries books and does not know what is on its back.

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾: books, and the book in Nabataean is called safar; Allah struck this as a parable for those who were given the Torah and then disbelieved.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾. The asfar are the books. Allah made the likeness of one who reads a book and does not follow what is in it like the donkey carrying the heavy book of Allah, not knowing what is in it. Then He said: ﴿Wretched is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah﴾ ... the verse.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's saying: ﴿like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾ he said: the asfar is the Torah, which the donkey carries on its back, just as copies of the Qur'an are carried on beasts; the likeness of a man who travels and carries his mushaf. He said: the donkey gains nothing from it while it carries it on its back; likewise these people gained nothing from it when they did not act upon it, though it had been given to them, just as this one gains nothing from it while it is on its back.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾ he says: books. The asfar is the plural of safr, and they are the great books.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Wretched is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah﴾

He says: wretched is this likeness, the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah, meaning His proofs and arguments. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ means, He, dhikruhu, says: and Allah does not grant success to the people who wronged themselves by disbelieving in the signs of their Lord.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say, O People of the Book who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews: ﴿Say: O you who are Jews﴾ ﴿if you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of other people﴾ other than you, ﴿then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ in your claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of other people. For God does not punish His allies; rather, He honours them and bestows favour upon them. And if you are right in what you say, then wish for death, so that you may rest from the hardship of this world, its cares and its griefs, and arrive at the spirit and bliss of the Gardens through death.

Ibn Zayd narrated to me, saying: Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Say: O you who are Jews﴾, "Say, O you who have repented, to the Jews." Moses said: ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾, meaning, "Indeed, we have repented to You."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 62, verse 7–8:

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ [62:7]

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And they will never wish for it﴾ means: the Jews will never wish for death, ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾ means: because of the sins they have earned in this world and the evil deeds they have committed. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ means: Allah has knowledge of those among His creation who wronged themselves, ruining them through their disbelief in Allah.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do"﴾ [62:8]

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾ — O Muhammad, to the Jews — ﴿Indeed, the death from which you flee﴾ — so you dislike it and refuse to wish for it — ﴿will surely meet you﴾ and descend upon you, ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ — then your Lord will return you, after your death, to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. As for "the witnessed": it means what is present and becomes manifest to the eye's sight, and is not hidden from the eyes of observers.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Qatadah recited: ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, and said: "Indeed Allah has humbled the son of Adam through death; I do not know it except that He raised it [the matter]." ﴿And He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ means: He will then inform you of the deeds you used to do in the world, the evil and the good, because He encompasses all of them. Then He will reward the doer of good for his goodness, and the doer of evil according to what he deserves.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 62, verse 7–8:

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ [62:7]

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And they will never wish for it﴾ means: the Jews will never wish for death, ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾ means: because of the sins they have earned in this world and the evil deeds they have committed. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ means: Allah has knowledge of those among His creation who wronged themselves, ruining them through their disbelief in Allah.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do"﴾ [62:8]

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾ — O Muhammad, to the Jews — ﴿Indeed, the death from which you flee﴾ — so you dislike it and refuse to wish for it — ﴿will surely meet you﴾ and descend upon you, ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ — then your Lord will return you, after your death, to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. As for "the witnessed": it means what is present and becomes manifest to the eye's sight, and is not hidden from the eyes of observers.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Qatadah recited: ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, and said: "Indeed Allah has humbled the son of Adam through death; I do not know it except that He raised it [the matter]." ﴿And He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ means: He will then inform you of the deeds you used to do in the world, the evil and the good, because He encompasses all of them. Then He will reward the doer of good for his goodness, and the doer of evil according to what he deserves.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers among His servants: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger. ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday﴾ This is the call, the summons to the Friday prayer, issued when the imam sits on the pulpit for the sermon. The meaning of the statement is: when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾, that is, go forth to the remembrance of Allah and act for Him. The original sense of "sa'y" (striving) in this context is action, and we have already cited the evidence for this earlier.

What we have said is also what the people of ta'wil (exegetes) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Shurahbil ibn Muslim al-Khawlani, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾. He said: "Strive in action, and striving is not walking."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾. And "sa'y", O son of Adam, is that you strive with your heart and your deeds, and it is the going forth to it.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, who said: Mughira informed me, from Ibrahim, that it was said to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "Ubayy recites it ﴿fa-s'aw﴾." He said: "Indeed he is the most knowledgeable of us in the abrogated (mansukh), but it is only fa-mdu (proceed)."

Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Sukkari narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said: "I never heard Umar recite it except as fa-mdu."

Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Hanzala narrated to us, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, who said: "Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite it: ﴿fa-mdu ila dhikri Allah﴾."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hanzala, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, that Umar ibn al-Khattab recited it: fa-mdu.

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Hanzala ibn Abi Sufyan al-Jumahi narrated to us, that he heard Salim ibn Abd Allah relate from his father that he heard Umar ibn al-Khattab recite ﴿idha nudiya li-l-salati min yawm al-jumu'a fa-mdu ila dhikri Allah﴾.

He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Salim ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar informed me that Abd Allah said: "Allah took Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and he did not recite this verse in which Allah mentions Friday, ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday﴾, except as: fa-mdu ila dhikri Allah."

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "Abd Allah used to recite it: 'fa-mdu ila dhikri Allah,' and he would say: 'If I had recited fa-s'aw, I would have striven until my cloak fell off.'"

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Sulayman, from Ibrahim, who said: Abd Allah said: "If striving were (meant), I would have striven until my cloak fell off." He said: "Rather, it is ﴿fa-mdu ila dhikri Allah﴾." He said: "Thus he used to recite it."

Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman al-Azdi narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya, that he recited it: ﴿fa-mdu ila dhikri Allah﴾.

Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya, that he recited it: ﴿fa-mdu ila dhikri Allah﴾.

Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: "It is for the free men."

Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from a man, from Masruq, who said: "It is at the time (of the prayer)."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from a man, from Masruq, regarding ﴿when the call is made for prayer﴾, who said: "It is at the time."

Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, who said: "It is at the resolve (azma) during the sermon, at the remembrance."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday﴾, who said: "The call at the remembrance is a resolve (azima)."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday﴾, who said: "The resolve at the remembrance, at the sermon."

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mughira and al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "If I had recited ﴿fa-s'aw﴾, I would have striven until my cloak fell off." And he used to recite it: ﴿fa-mdu ila dhikri Allah﴾.

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "He recited it: ﴿fa-mdu﴾." Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Hayyan, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾, who said: "Sa'y is action."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "I asked him about the words of Allah: ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾, and he said: When you hear the first caller, respond to it and hasten, and do not delay." He said: "In the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) there were only two calls to prayer: a call when he sat on the pulpit, and a call when the prayer was established. And this latter one is something people introduced afterwards." He said: "Trade is not lawful for him when he hears the call that takes place before the imam when he sits on the pulpit and recites ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade﴾." He said: "He did not command them to leave anything except it, trade being forbidden, then permitted to them when they finish the prayer." He said: "And sa'y is to hasten toward it, to come toward it."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "In the reading (harf) of Ibn Mas'ud it is: ﴿idha nudiya li-l-salati min yawm al-jumu'a fa-mdu ila dhikri Allah﴾."

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾: "Sa'y is action." Allah said: ﴿Indeed your striving is diverse﴾.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿and leave off trade﴾

It means: abandon buying and selling when the call is made for prayer at the sermon.

Al-Dahhak used to say regarding this:

Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "When the sun declines, buying and selling become forbidden."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday﴾, who said: "When the sun declines, buying and selling become forbidden."

Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: "Some people used to sit in the Baqi' of al-Zubayr, buying and selling when the call to prayer on Friday was made, and they would not rise. So this was revealed: ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday﴾." As for the remembrance to which Allah, blessed and exalted, commanded His believing servants to strive, it is said that it is the imam's admonition in his sermon.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday﴾, who said: "The resolve at the remembrance, at the sermon."

Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: Abdan narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah informed us, saying: Mansur, a man from the people of Kufa, informed us, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾. "It is the admonition of the imam; when the prayer has been concluded, afterwards..."

* * *

And His saying: ﴿That is better for you, if you only knew﴾

It means: your striving, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, toward the remembrance of Allah, and leaving off trade, is better for you than buying and selling at that time, if you know your own interests and harms.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿min yawm al-jumu'a﴾. The majority of the readers of the major cities recited it: ﴿al-jumu'a﴾ with a damma on the mim and the jim, except al-A'mash, who recited it with the mim lightened.

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is what the readers of the major cities hold, due to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative readers upon it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 62, verse 10:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may be successful.﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When the Friday prayer (salat al-jumu'ah) has been concluded on Friday, then disperse throughout the land if you wish; this is a concession (rukhsah) from Allah to you in that matter.

What we have said regarding this is also what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Mujahid that he said: It is a concession, meaning His words: ﴿So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land﴾.

* I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: ﴿So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land﴾: This is a permission from Allah; whoever wishes may go out, and whoever wishes may sit.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Allah permitted them when they finished the prayer: ﴿So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah﴾, so I have made it lawful for you.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿and seek from the bounty of Allah﴾

There is related from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the interpretation of this, that:

* Al-Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Mu'afa ibn Ya'qub al-Mawsili narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir al-Sa'igh of Mosul narrated to us, from Abu Khalaf, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding His words: ﴿So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah﴾: "It is not for seeking worldly gain, but for visiting a sick person, attending a funeral, and visiting a brother for the sake of Allah."

It is possible that His words ﴿and seek from the bounty of Allah﴾ mean: and seek from the bounty of Allah, in whose hand are the keys of His treasures, for your worldly life and your Hereafter.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿and remember Allah often that you may be successful﴾

He says: Remember Allah by praising Him and thanking Him for what He has bestowed upon you of success in performing His obligations, so that you may prosper, attaining your requests with your Lord and reaching eternity in His gardens.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 62, verse 11:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it and leave you standing.  Say: "What is with Allah is better than diversion and than trade, and Allah is the best of providers."﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And when the believers see a caravan (ʿayr) of trade or a diversion ﴿they rush off to it﴾," meaning: they hasten toward the trade. ﴿And they leave you standing﴾ says to the Prophet ﷺ: "and they leave you, O Muhammad, standing upon the pulpit." That is because the trade they saw, for which the people dispersed, and left the Prophet ﷺ standing, was oil brought by Dihyah ibn Khalifah from Syria.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ismail al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: Dihyah ibn Khalifah arrived with a trade of oil from Syria while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the sermon on Friday. When they saw it, they stood up toward it at al-Baqi', fearing they would be forestalled from reaching it. He said: then the verse was revealed: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it and leave you standing.﴾

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Qurrah, regarding ﴿when it is called for prayer on the day of Friday﴾, who said: Dihyah al-Kalbi came with a trade while the Prophet ﷺ was standing in prayer on Friday, so they left the Prophet ﷺ and went out to it, and then the verse was revealed: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it and leave you standing﴾, until the end of the surah.

Abu Husayn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: ʿAbthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Friday prayer when a caravan carrying food passed by, so the people went out except for twelve men, and then the verse of the Friday prayer was revealed."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, who said: al-Hasan said: The people of Medina were afflicted with hunger and high prices, so a caravan arrived while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the sermon on Friday. They heard of it and went out while the Prophet ﷺ was standing, just as Allah, mighty and majestic, said.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it and leave you standing﴾: "A trade came and they turned to it, leaving the Prophet ﷺ standing. And when they saw a diversion and play ﴿Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and than trade, and Allah is the best of providers.﴾"

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it﴾, who said: "They were men who would rise to their water-camels and to travel, seeking trade."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: "While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was addressing the people on Friday, they began slipping away and standing up until only a small group remained. He said: 'How many are you?' They counted themselves, and they were twelve men and a woman. Then he stood on the second Friday and began addressing them." Sufyan said: I know only that in his narration: "and he admonished them and reminded them, and they began slipping away and standing up until only a small group remained. He said: 'How many are you?' They counted themselves, and they were twelve men and a woman. Then he stood on the third Friday, and they began slipping away and standing up until only a small group remained. He said: 'How many are you?' They counted themselves, and they were twelve men and a woman. He said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, if the last of you were to follow the first of you, the valley would blaze with fire upon you.'" And Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it and leave you standing﴾.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿they rush off to it and leave you standing﴾, who said: "If the last of them were to follow the first of them, the valley would blaze with fire upon them."

He said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, Maʿmar said, Qatadah said: No one remained with the Prophet ﷺ that day except twelve men and a woman with them.

Muhammad ibn ʿUmarah al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Salim and Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, regarding His words: ﴿and they leave you standing﴾, who said: "A caravan arrived and they rushed to it, and no one remained with the Prophet ﷺ except twelve men."

ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Amuli narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Husayn, from Salim, from Jabir: "The Prophet ﷺ was delivering the sermon standing on Friday when a caravan came from Syria, and the people turned toward it until only twelve men remained." He said: this verse was revealed concerning Friday: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it and leave you standing﴾.

As for the diversion, it has been disputed what kind of diversion it was. Some said it was a kabar (a drum; or a drum with two heads; or a drum with one face, in the dialect of the people of Kufa; or a small drum) and flutes.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn ʿAskar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: "When the young women married, they would pass by with the kabar and flutes, and leave the Prophet ﷺ standing upon the pulpit and rush off to it; so Allah revealed: (And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it)."

Others said: it was a drum.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The diversion is the drum."

al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Ashyab narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Najih mentioned, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, from Mujahid, that the diversion is the drum.

What is most correct in this matter is the report we narrated from Jabir, because he witnessed the affair of those people and their gatherings.

As for His saying: ﴿Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and than trade﴾, His praise says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say to them, O Muhammad: what is with Allah of reward, for whoever sits listening to the sermon and admonition of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on Friday until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finishes from it, is better for him than the diversion and the trade toward which they rush." ﴿And Allah is the best of providers﴾ means: Allah is the best provider; so turn toward Him in seeking your provision, and ask Him alone to widen His bounty upon you, apart from anyone else.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Jumu'ah.
